discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `19e5855e1`. `GitHubConnector.refresh` now adds each scope's line to the live snapshot for that repository#branch after its awaits, instead of each refresh building and assigning its own snapshot. `pendingPr` lets `reviews` reuse the in-flight PR fetch, and `latestKey` drops a refresh whose repository#branch is not that of the latest refresh to start; connectors.test.ts covers scopes refreshing at once.

Fixed in `d23386884`. `pruneSessionStates` still screens files with the async `stat`. For an expired file it now re-checks with `statSync` and removes it with `rmSync` with no await in between, so a state file rewritten while the first stat was pending is kept, as `session-state.test.ts` covers. A write from another process that lands between those two calls can still be lost, because there is no unlink-if-unchanged.

Fixed in `d11e7aca0`. `pruneSessionStates` now removes an expired file through `removeIfUnchanged`: it renames the file aside (atomic, so no write can interleave) and deletes it only if it is still the version whose age was checked (same inode, mtime and size); a version written since goes back with `linkSync`, which fails rather than overwrite a write that landed after the rename. `session-state.test.ts` covers a write after the last check and one that lands while a newer version is held aside.

Fixed in b33dc598d: the bind cleanup now bumps the bind generation before it detaches, so a `plugin_ui_get` still pending when the pane unmounts never attaches the chat it left. A one-key Send that was already made still reaches that chat.

Fixed in f83618bd27. `begin()` now only stages the new epoch. `activate()` promotes it once the replacement session is resident. Until then the resident session keeps its slot state, viewers and UI chain, and keeps serving invokes. A start that fails releases only its staged epoch, so a failed reopen leaves the working chat's suggestions as they were. `clearPlugin` also takes the epoch now, so a plugin that fails while the replacement is starting can't clear the resident copy.

Covered by "serves the resident session while a same-id start is pending and after it fails" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, plus the staging cases in `store.test.ts` and `service.teardown.test.ts`.

Valid, and new to this PR: before the pre-run guard, a stopped one-shot session reached `agent.run` on a shutting-down runtime instead of failing deterministically. Fixed in "keep a stopped one-shot session out of the failure teardown": once teardown has started it owns the status and the `ended` event, so the catches in `startSession` and `runTurn` no longer route a non-interactive failure through `failSession`; `startSession` resolves without a result and `runTurn` resolves `undefined`. Two tests cover the start turn and a seeded session's follow-up turn, asserting a single `cancelled`, a single `ended` and a single `agent.shutdown`.

`executeTurn` has already counted this turn in `turnsInFlight` before it calls this function, so a teardown that has begun is already visible through `hasActiveTurn`. This check asks the same question again in different words. The check after `markTurnRunning` at line 2146 is needed, because the `await`s between them can let teardown start. Please remove the first check and keep the second.

Removed. It was only there to keep a turn from creating the row after teardown had skipped the status write; with persistence first, teardown finds the row creation to wait on and writes `cancelled` onto it, so the check after `markTurnRunning` is the only one left.

Valid, fixed in 249fa9dec. After the awaits, spawnTerminalTab returns if the tab is no longer starting (before touching its disposed xterm). The same gap existed while terminal_spawn itself is in flight, so if the tab was closed by the time the spawn returns, it now sends terminal_kill for the new shell. Checked live that closing tabs, including add-then-close in quick succession, leaves no stray shells.

Agreed, fixed in 34056fc61. After waiting for Hub startup, `handleCommand` now rejects the command if its connection is no longer in `ctx.wsClients`. The close handler has already run by then, so nothing else could cancel work started for that connection. Covered by `drops a waiting command whose connection closed during startup` in `commands-hub-startup.test.ts`.

+			} finally {

+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	private ensurePolling(): void {

The start now uses the model the composer showed at submit time, snapshotted in `beginCloudTask` before any await, instead of refreshing recommendations first. The composer warms the recommendation cache once so the label moves off the built-in fallback before the next submit. Test: "starts the sandbox on the model the composer showed, even when a fresher recommendation lands first".

Fixed in 4e4d602c4. The PUT is now always sent (matching what main does for the ClinePass path), so an account another client moved is restored. Only the cloud teardown is gated on the cached account actually changing, since that is what scoped the cloud state. `account-service.test.ts` "restores the server account without tearing down cloud state when the cached account already matches" covers it.

This is inherent in the distributed nature of the system and is a gap we can only narrow but not close in the current design. We will accept this limitation for now. If an error arises, it probably relates to something the user did recently, and the recovery path is pretty straightforward: Switch organizations and try the operation again. Not to mention, only a few users have organizations.

Implemented in `84db143`.

The response is claimed before the first asynchronous delivery step, so a second submission cannot resolve the same question. It is routed through the normal follow-up path while the claimed response continues delivering its attachments. I kept the session identity check and retained a per-attempt validity token so cancellation, replacement questions, delivery failures, and retries remain safe: an old callback cannot become current again after a retry, and a failed attempt releases only its own claim.

The focused VS Code suites cover the overlap, cancellation, failure/retry, and stale-callback cases and pass; SDK typecheck also passes. The separate display fix keeps the original pending-question text in the submitted event while preserving the expanded model prompt.

Implemented in commit `84db143`.

The pending ask response is now claimed synchronously before attachment preparation begins. While that claim is in flight, another submission cannot resolve the same `ask_question`; it falls through to the normal follow-up path instead. The claim is tied to the individual delivery attempt, so cancellation or replacement of the question invalidates older callbacks, while a delivery error releases only its own claim and leaves the original response retryable.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed. The record is now forgotten only when `CloudSessionHost.whenTurnAccepted()` resolves, i.e. when the Hub reports run activity for the session or `runTurn` returns, not when the send is launched. If a host exits after acceptance but before forgetting, recovery inspects the sandbox and leaves it if it has taken a turn. Covered by `keeps a provisioning sandbox recorded until the sandbox accepts its first turn`.

Good catch, fixed in 98d674cfa. shutdownSession now deletes the slot only when it still points at the runtime being shut down, the same guard releaseSessionRuntime already had. Regression test: a stop stalled in the resident's agent shutdown while a same-id start registers the replacement; the replacement stays reachable afterwards (fails with session_not_found without the guard).

Valid, fixed in a65115d1c. The pending-start entry in sessionStarts now records an abort issued while the start is in flight; a turn that waited on that start completes as aborted (done event, aborted result) without running on the replacement. The agent runtime ignores an abort before run() starts, so this has to be decided at the host before the turn is dispatched. Regression test: B sends during A's rebuild, aborts before it finishes, the turn resolves aborted with neither agent's run called, and the replacement takes the next turn normally.

Good catch, fixed in efd698c2e. The replacement is now built first and takes over the map entry (the same shape as pre-#14501), and the old runtime object is released afterwards with a guard so it cannot evict the newcomer. There is no longer a window without a resident session, and a failed rebuild leaves the idle resident untouched (test added).

Fixed in 17ff65c7b. The old runtime is now released in a finally, so it is torn down whether the rebuild resolves or throws (including the case where the replacement claimed the slot and then its initial turn failed and removed it). The release guard only deletes the map entry when it still points at the old object, so a live replacement is left in place; a failed rebuild leaves no resident, and the next start rebuilds from disk. Test updated to assert the resident is released (not stranded) when the rebuild's build throws.

Confirmed and fixed in 823a53c05. startResolvedSession wrote usageBySession/aggregateUsageBySession before building the runtime, so a bootstrap failure had already overwritten the resident's totals. Rather than snapshot-and-restore in startSession, the two writes now sit next to this.sessions.set(...), so a start that never registers leaves no host-level state behind (nothing between the old location and registration read those maps). Test seeds the resident with usage via a rebuild carrying metrics, then fails a rebuild with no history and asserts the totals are intact; it fails on the previous commit with usage reset to 0.

Valid, thanks. Fixed in cd3582cca: host replacement now chains onto the previous host promise so concurrent callers serialize, and a stale host is shut down and reloaded exactly once. Verified against the real goal plugin: three concurrent cold calls spawned one sandbox, and two concurrent calls after bumping the plugin mtime replaced it once with no leaked process.
